newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Feb real earnings rose 2.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Feb real earnings rose 2.4 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, rose 2.4 percent in February, the Labor Department said Wednesday.
The February increase followed a revised 1.7 percent drop in January real average weekly earnings.
Previously, the department reported that January real earnings fell 2.0 percent.
February's increase matched Wall Street economists' projection of a 2.4 percent rise.

The February rise stems from a 2.3 percent increase in average weekly hours and a 0.2 percent gain in average hourly earnings. These increases were partially offset by a 0.2 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, the department said.
Real average weekly earnings in February were 1.9 percent above their February 1996 level, it said.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $261.37 in February, versus $255.23 in January and $255.68 in February 1996.
In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $423.15 in February, compared with $412.45 in January and $401.93 in February last year.
The Labor Department said the 2.4 percent rise in February real earnings was the biggest monthly gain since a 2.3 percent increase in February 1982.
